QB, Cincinnati, 6’4 208

Strengths:

  • Very good arm. Throws passes with plenty of zip and uses good touch when needed. Throws a very good looking ball.

  • Generally an accurate passer on short and intermediate routes.

  • Usually has good footwork, but needs more consistency.

  • Pocket passer, but enough mobility to escape if need be.

  • Moves through his progressions quickly.

Weaknesses:

  • Throwing motion could use some speeding up.

  • Good footwork at times but needs more consistency. Throws too many off his back foot.

  • Inconsistent accuracy on deep passes.

  • Decision making questionable at times. Gunslinger mentality but needs to know when to dial it back.

  • Played almost exclusively in shotgun. Will need to learn to play under center.

Overall: Kiel finally got his chance to shine in Cincinnati, and took advantage. He put up good numbers and made some very impressive plays with his excellent arm and touch. However, he needs to be more careful with the ball and improve his mechanics. Right now I see him as a day two choice, though if he improves he has the potential to be a first rounder.

Good write up. I think UC and Kiel are poised for a huge season. Their offense will put up video game numbers. That is, if Kiel can stay healthy. We used him too much with the option run and banged up his ribs, plagued him for the later half of the season. If he's healthy, he'll be one of the top QBs this year.

He definitely has the tools to be a first rounder with a big arm and generally accurate with the occasional wild deep pass. He just needs more reps and to work on being more careful with his passes. Right now it's looking like a very strong quarterback class. Hackenberg is my favorite so far, but he definitely needs to show major strides with footwork and accuracy. Cook and Goff also look like very solid first rounders, while Kiel and Cardale have a chance to go high as well.

I saw a mock draft for next year right after this past years draft was over and I believe it had Kiel in the 15-20 range. I was surprised by that. I think he needs to improve quite a bit before he can be tossed around as a name going in the first round.
I agree, he definitely needs move development. This was his first real season and while he flashed some brilliant play he needs more consistency in his mechanics and decision making.
